about: Hand-labelled passages for three literary devices: antithesis, tricolon (the rule of three) and anaphora. One annotator labelled every item on 2026-10-26; the labels are unvalidated. A 'lookalike' item carries a surface shape a detector might read (not ... but, a list of three, repeated openers) without the device. Sources are public-domain works, proverbs, or sentences written for this fixture ('constructed').

definitions.antithesis: two contrasting ideas set against each other in a balanced or mirrored construction, with or without a negation
definitions.tricolon: three parallel members used for rhythm or emphasis; a plain factual list of three items is not the device
definitions.anaphora: the same word or words repeated at the start of three or more successive clauses or sentences for emphasis
